subject: c-act
title: C.ACT.------POL.SIGN.
description: Diagram in AE(PD)-7 (Aspect Essence / Perception Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's analysis of CORE (Congress of Racial Equality) and sixties alternative-functionalism: 'As early as 1964 one could view the solidification of dynamic functionalism in American social reality. This was especially true for the emergence of alternative functionalism — as related to the reality position of poor and disenfranchised Americans.' (C)C-ACT (the concept of composite activism) is crossed with POL-SIGN (political significance): the question is what composite-activism produces when crossed with political-significance — composite-activism being CORE's mode (multiple groups, multiple cities, multiple issues unified by structural concern). PROG-SIGN (progressional significance) feeds in from the upper-left. C-ACT itself sits centrally at the top. RE-ST (restructuralism) anchors the upper-right output. EXP-DY (experimental dynamics) and DEC (decision) form the upper-center cluster. INFO-DS (information descent) sits below the crossing line. POL-SIGN appears with GRAD (gradualism) as the partner. PHY-U-P (physical universe particulars) hangs on the right output via a *dashed* edge from POL-SIGN to GRAD — conditional. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) anchors the lower-center via another dashed edge. Structural argument: composite-activism crossed with political-significance produces restructuralism as the primary output, with physical-universe-particulars as a *conditional* (dashed) downstream of gradualism. The dashed edges expose Braxton's structural diagnostic: composite-activism in the early sixties produced *real* restructuralism precisely because it did not commit to gradualism — gradualism's link to physical-universe-particulars was held dashed (conditional), reserving the option for non-gradual change. The diagram is the structural reason early-sixties activism worked: experimental-dynamics and decision were upper upstreams (not gradualism), and restructuralism was the productive output.
